primary_topics: Remarks by CJP on behalf of Cardinal Tagle and the Manila Cathedral-Basilica Foundation at a donor appreciation event, June 4, 2015
Tribute to the Cathedral's benefactors: P186 million cash + P14 million non-cash = P200 million total; many gave more than asked or committed; many gave without being asked and requested anonymity
Ramon S. Ang: top cash contributor -- immediately agreed to an unquantified amount 'without a letter of request, without an architectural plan and without an estimate of the total funds needed'

Bert and Sylvia Lina: original donors of 14 Carillon Bells (December 2010); after CJP's European tour, Bert declined to add 9 bells and instead gave a completely new set of 23 computerized Carillon Bells from the Netherlands -- 'Church bells are the voice of God'
sub_topics: Cardinal Rosales' original initiative: asked Ambassador Tita de Villa to summon Foundation officers to address the belfry's structural integrity; brought down the heavy bells; installed 14 lighter Carillon Bells in December 2010
Cardinal Rosales' absence: not feeling well; greeted in absentia
Total donations: cash totalling over P186 million; non-cash equivalents about P14 million; grand total about P200 million; 'many of you gave more than what we asked, and more than what you committed'

Ramon Ang story: two years before the event, CJP mentioned the Cathedral restoration dream to Ang 'without any idea how much would be needed' (no as-built plans, no architectural plan); Ang 'immediately agreed to the figure I quoted even without a letter of request, without an architectural plan and without an estimate of the total funds needed'

Bert Lina's 14 -> 23 bells upgrade: Bert and Sylvia gave 14 Carillon Bells before the major renovations; after CJP toured European cathedrals and discovered best sets have 23 bells, he suggested adding 9; Bert refused to add 9 -- 'I will not give nine bells. I will give a complete new set of 23 bells because, if I just add nine new ones, they may not be in tune with the existing 14. I must give the best to our Cathedral. Church bells are the voice of God.'; ordered computerized 23-bell set from the Netherlands; air freighted to arrive for inauguration December 11, 2014
Anonymous donors: many requested not to be identified -- 'because you said quite correctly that anyway our Lord knows. Indeed, your reward is better given in heaven than here on earth'

Heavenly thank-you vision: 'the appreciation and thanks you will receive today is only preliminary to the greater and final one waiting for you at the heavenly gate, when on that inevitable day, our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, together with His Mother, Mary the Immaculate Conception, would greet you by spreading His divine arms, saying: Thank you, thank you for helping restore the Manila Cathedral. Well done on your temporary sojourn on earth. Welcome to your permanent home in heaven! Alleluia!!!'

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered June 4, 2015 on behalf of Cardinal Tagle and the Manila Cathedral-Basilica Foundation at a donor appreciation event, this address by CJP thanks benefactors whose total contributions reached approximately P200 million (P186 million cash + P14 million non-cash) -- with many giving more than asked or committed, and many requesting anonymity ('because you said quite correctly that anyway our Lord knows'). Two centerpiece stories: first, Ramon Ang -- the top cash contributor -- immediately agreed to fund the restoration when CJP mentioned the dream two years earlier, 'without a letter of request, without an architectural plan and without an estimate of the total funds needed,' giving based entirely on trust. Second, Bert and Sylvia Lina, who donated the original 14 Carillon Bells in December 2010; after CJP toured European cathedrals and discovered that the best sets have 23 bells, he suggested adding 9; Bert refused: 'I will not give nine bells. I will give a complete new set of 23 bells because, if I just add nine new ones, they may not be in tune with the existing 14. I must give the best to our Cathedral. Church bells are the voice of God.' Bert ordered a computerized 23-bell set from the Netherlands and air freighted it for the December 11, 2014 inauguration. CJP frames the donor appreciation as preliminary to the greater heavenly one: on the inevitable day each donor knocks at the pearly gate, 'our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, together with His Mother, Mary the Immaculate Conception, would greet you by spreading His divine arms, saying: Thank you, thank you for helping restore the Manila Cathedral. Well done on your temporary sojourn on earth. Welcome to your permanent home in heaven! Alleluia!!!'
